# Input Widgets

## Input Widgets

- Common inputs: `selectInput()`, `sliderInput()`, `checkboxInput()`, `textInput()`, `dateInput()`
- Grouped inputs: `radioButtons()`, `checkboxGroupInput()`
- Dynamic UI with `renderUI()` and `uiOutput()`


## Input Widgets: Common structure

- First argument -- `inputId` -- is the identifier: connects front end with back end
  - if UI is "name" then `input$name`
  - name should only be letters, numbers and underscores and it should be unique
- Second argument: "label" a human-readable label for control. 
- Third parameter: "value" e.g. default value
- Remaining parameters are unique to the control

```{r eval=F}
sliderInput("min", "Minimum", value = 50, min = 0, max = 100)
```

## Input Widgets: Free text

```{r eval = F}
ui <- fluidPage(
  textInput("name", "What's your name?"),
  passwordInput("password", "What's your password?"),
  textAreaInput("story", "Tell me about yourself", rows = 3)
)
```

## Input Widgets: Numeric inputs


```{r eval = F}
ui <- fluidPage(
  numericInput("num", "Number one", value = 0, min = 0, max = 100),
  sliderInput("num2", "Number two", value = 50, min = 0, max = 100),
  sliderInput("rng", "Range", value = c(10, 20), min = 0, max = 100)
)
```

## Input Widgets: Dates

```{r eval = F}
ui <- fluidPage(
  dateInput("dob", "When were you born?"),
  dateRangeInput("holiday", "When do you want to go on vacation next?")
)
```


## Input Widgets: Limited choices

```{r eval = F}
animals <- c("dog", "cat", "mouse", "bird", "other")

ui <- fluidPage(
  selectInput("state", "What's your favourite state?", state.name),
  radioButtons("animal", "What's your favourite animal?", animals), # one selection only
  checkboxGroupInput("animal", "What animals do you like?", animals), # multiple selections allowed
  checkboxInput("restart", "Restart?") # yes / no questions
)
```

`selectInput()` can allow multiple selections (`multiple = TRUE`).

## Input Widgets: File uploads

```{r eval = F}
ui <- fluidPage(
  fileInput("upload", NULL)
)
```

## Input Widgets: Action buttons

```{r eval = F}
ui <- fluidPage(
  actionButton("click", "Click me!")
)
```

Paired with `observeEvent()` or `eventReactive()` in your server function.

# Dynamic UI

## Dynamic UI

- Dynamic UI allows you to change the interface based on user input
- Useful for customizing inputs, showing/hiding elements, and building flexible dashboards
- Give more information to the user when you are working on sophisticated applications.
- Make it easier to select from a long list of possible options, through step-by-step filtering. 

## Dynamic UI: Key Functions

There are three key techniques for creating dynamic user interfaces:

- `update` family of functions modifies parameters of input controls.
- `tabsetPanel()` conditionally shows and hides parts of the user interface.
- `uiOutput()` and `renderUI()` generates selected parts of the user interface.


## Dynamic UI: Updating inputs {.columns-2}

- `update` family of functions: modify an input after it has been created.
- Every input control, e.g. `textInput()`, is paired with an update function, e.g. `updateTextInput()`, that allows you to modify the control after it has been created.
- Example app: two inputs that control the range (the min and max) of another input, a slider. 
- Use `observeEvent()` to trigger `updateSliderInput()` whenever the min or max inputs change.
- See `3_app.R`
- Update functions take name of the input as the the `inputId` argument.

```{r eval = F}
ui <- fluidPage(
  numericInput("min", "Minimum", 0),
  numericInput("max", "Maximum", 3),
  sliderInput("n", "n", min = 0, max = 3, value = 1)
)
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$min, {
    updateSliderInput(inputId = "n", min = input$min)
  })
  observeEvent(input$max, {
    updateSliderInput(inputId = "n", max = input$max)
  })
}
```


## Dynamic UI: Simple uses {.columns-2}

- Simplest uses of the update functions: provide small conveniences for the user. 
- For example, make it easy to reset parameters back to their initial value. 
- Combine `actionButton()`, `observeEvent()` and `updateSliderInput()`.


```{r eval = F}
ui <- fluidPage(
  sliderInput("x1", "x1", 0, min = -10, max = 10),
  sliderInput("x2", "x2", 0, min = -10, max = 10),
  sliderInput("x3", "x3", 0, min = -10, max = 10),
  actionButton("reset", "Reset")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$reset, {
    updateSliderInput(inputId = "x1", value = 0)
    updateSliderInput(inputId = "x2", value = 0)
    updateSliderInput(inputId = "x3", value = 0)
  })
}
```


## Dynamic UI: Simple uses {.columns-2}

Tweak the text of an action button so you know exactly what it's going to do.

```{r eval = F}
ui <- fluidPage(
  numericInput("n", "Simulations", 10),
  actionButton("simulate", "Simulate")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$n, {
    label <- paste0("Simulate ", input$n, " times")
    updateActionButton(inputId = "simulate", label = label)
  })
}
```



## Dynamic UI: Hierarchical select boxes {.columns-2}

- Interactive drill down across multiple categories
- Natural hierarchy in the data:
  - Each response modality contains multiple participants and images.
  - Each participant has provided data for some images.
  - Half of the participants were familiarised with one set of images, the other half with the other set of images.

```{r echo = F}
read_csv("../../data/spellname.csv") %>% glimpse()
```



## Dynamic UI: Hierarchical select boxes {.columns-2}

I want to create a user interface where you can:
  - Select a response modality 
  - Select all responses of a participant
  - (could then also select image within participant, etc)

The essence of the UI is simple: Create two select boxes and one output plot. The choices for the participants will be dynamically generated, so I set `choices = NULL`.

See `5_app.R`

```{r eval = F}
# Create user interface
ui <- fluidPage(
  selectInput("mod", "Response modality", choices = unique(spellname$modality)),
  selectInput("ppt", "Participants", choices = NULL),
  plotOutput("plot")
)

# Create server
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  sn_mod <- reactive({
    filter(spellname, modality == input$mod) %>%
      select(-modality)
  })

  observeEvent(sn_mod(), {
    choices <- unique(sn_mod()$ppt_id)
    updateSelectInput(inputId = "ppt", choices = choices)
  })

  ppt <- reactive({
    req(input$ppt)
    filter(sn_mod(), ppt_id == input$ppt)
  })

  # [...]
}

```

## Dynamic UI: Dynamic visibility {.columns-2}

- Selectively show and hide parts of the UI. 
- Concealing optional UI with a **tabset**.
- Show and hide UI as needed, without having to re-generate it from scratch.
- Use tabset panel with hidden tabs.
- Use `updateTabsetPanel()` to switch tabs from the server.


```{r eval = F}
ui <- fluidPage(
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      selectInput("controller", "Show", choices = paste0("panel", 1:3))
    ),
    mainPanel(
      tabsetPanel(
        id = "switcher",
        type = "hidden",
        tabPanelBody("panel1", "Panel 1 content"),
        tabPanelBody("panel2", "Panel 2 content"),
        tabPanelBody("panel3", "Panel 3 content")
      )
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$controller, {
    updateTabsetPanel(inputId = "switcher", selected = input$controller)
  })
}
```





## Dynamic UI: Conditional UI 

- App `6_app.R`: simulate from the normal and exponential distributions. 
- Each distribution has different parameters so we’ll need some way to show different controls for different distributions. 
- Unique UI for each distribution will appear in its own `tabPanel()`.
- Arrange the two tabs into a `tabsetPanel()`.
- Add in another parameter: the sample size which is currently hard coded as `n`



## Dynamic UI: Wizard interface {.columns-2}

- "Wizard" (`7_app.R`) : interface that collects a bunch of information by spreading it across multiple pages. 
- We embed action buttons within each "page", making it easy to go forward and back. 
- `switch_page()` reduces the amount of duplication in the server code. 


```{r eval = F}
ui <- fluidPage(
  tabsetPanel(
    id = "wizard",
    type = "hidden",
    tabPanel("page_1",
      "Welcome!",
      actionButton("page_12", "next")
    ),
    tabPanel("page_2",
      "Only one page to go",
      actionButton("page_21", "prev"),
      actionButton("page_23", "next")
    ),
    tabPanel("page_3",
      "You're done!",
      actionButton("page_32", "prev")
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  switch_page <- function(i) {
    updateTabsetPanel(inputId = "wizard", selected = paste0("page_", i))
  }

  observeEvent(input$page_12, switch_page(2))
  observeEvent(input$page_21, switch_page(1))
  observeEvent(input$page_23, switch_page(3))
  observeEvent(input$page_32, switch_page(2))
}
```


## Exercise

Create an app that plots `ggplot(diamonds, aes(carat))` but allows the user to choose which geom to use: `geom_histogram()`, `geom_freqpoly()`, or `geom_density()`. Use a hidden tabset to allow the user to select different arguments depending on the geom: `geom_histogram()` and `geom_freqpoly()` have a `binwidth` argument; `geom_density()` has a `bw` (bandwidth) argument. Use slider input for `binwidth` and `bw`.


## Dynamic UI: Creating UI with code

- **Update** functions only allow you to change existing inputs, and a **tabset** only works if you have a fixed and known set of possible combinations. 
- Sometimes you need to create different types or numbers of inputs (or outputs), depending on other inputs. 
- So far, we have created a UI with code **before* the app started.
- We will now create and modify UI while app is running.

- `uiOutput()` inserts a placeholder in your ui. This leaves a "hole" that your server code can later fill in.
- `renderUI()` is called within `server()` to fill in the placeholder with dynamically generated UI.


## Dynamic UI: Creating UI with code {.columns-2}

See `8_app.R`




```{r eval = F}

ui <- fluidPage(
  textInput("label", "label"),
  selectInput("type", "type", c("slider", "numeric")),
  uiOutput("numeric")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$numeric <- renderUI({
    if (input$type == "slider") {
      sliderInput("dynamic", input$label, value = 0, min = 0, max = 10)
    } else {
      numericInput("dynamic", input$label, value = 0, min = 0, max = 10)
    }
  })
}

```

## Dynamic UI: Dynamic filtering

- Dynamically filter any data frame. 
- Each numeric variable gets a range slider and each factor variable will get a multi-select, so if a data frame has three numeric variables and two factors, the app will have three sliders and two select boxes.
- See `9_app.R`
- Adapt this code for another dataset:
  - Use `palmerpenguins::penguins`
  - Then instead of showing a table (or in addition to), create a scatterplot that includes at least two numeric variables.





## Exercise








## Filtering by a user-selected column

Update UI filter (`sliderInput()`) depending on which variable was selected?

```{r eval = F}

ui <- fluidPage(
  selectInput("var", "Choose variable:", choices = names(data)),
  uiOutput("filterUI"),
)

server <- function(input, output){
 # Dynamically generate filter input based on selected variable
  output$filterUI <- renderUI({
    req(input$var)
    var_data <- data[[input$var]]
    
    sliderInput("filterVal", 
                paste("Filter", input$var),
                min = min(var_data), 
                max = max(var_data),
                value = c(min(var_data), 
                          max(var_data)))
  })
  
}


```




## Filtering by a user-selected column

Base R

```{r eval = F}
data[input$var > input$varRange[1] & input$var < input$varRange[2],]
```

`tidyverse` functions need `!!sym(input$var)` as in 

```{r eval = F}
filter(data, 
       !!sym(input$var) > input$varRange[1] & 
       !!sym(input$var) < input$varRange[2])
```
